findings.reason: the plan should state whether it extends `reconcile_catalog_edit_origins` or supersedes it, and cite the landed evidence before proposing a new rule.
findings.text: `reconcile_catalog_edit_origins` already derives `origin` from surviving generation evidence (StandardNameSource.source_type: `derived`→'derived', `dd`/`signals`→'pipeline', else unset), is idempotent with a dry-run, and records one `lineage_reconciliation` change row per identity — the exact §3 design; the plan cites none of it, nor the run already recorded in docs/evidence/sn-lifecycle-integrity/catalog-edit-origin.md (1179 pipeline / 246 derived / 671 unset), so it risks re-deriving a mechanism that exists.

findings.reason: §4 must record that the guard has landed and scope itself to the residual (a test asserting the refusal, if absent) rather than re-proposing the guard.
findings.text: §4 ("the import path must lose the ability to clear or overwrite `origin` and `status`") is already implemented: `record_catalog_import_provenance` reduces caller payloads to {id, catalog_commit_sha}, refuses any payload carrying `origin`/`status` (catalog_import.py:73–84), and `guard_catalog_write_payloads`→`protection.refuse_pipeline_authority_loss` (protection.py:183) refuses a whole batch that would null or replace pipeline authority (catalog_import.py:61–63, 110–124); the plan presents this as work to do.

findings.reason: without the justification the plan commissions a second origin writer the graph cannot distinguish from the first.
findings.text: the plan's §3 recovery rule would sit beside `reconcile_catalog_edit_origins`, which already reads surviving provenance and writes origin, but the plan never says why that function cannot be extended (its evidence set could be widened to `model`/`generated_at`/`chain_length`/`LLMCost` in place).

findings.reason: a second origin writer and a second import-guard path drift from the owners already carrying the protection, and rejections already measured at these sites.
findings.text: the plan duplicates two shared mechanisms instead of extending the owners: origin recovery, owned by `imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:13875` (`reconcile_catalog_edit_origins`), and the catalog-import authority guard, owned by `imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_import.py:52` and `imas_codex/standard_names/protection.py:183` (`refuse_pipeline_authority_loss`); also relevant is `provenance_rebuild.rebuild_provenance` (provenance_rebuild.py:567), which already restores the source topology §3 would key on.

findings.reason: the plan should reuse `FOR_STANDARD_NAME`/`automatic_deletion_protections` rather than materialize its own generation-evidence joins.
findings.text: the plan's §2 evidence plan (LLMCost → pipeline-generated) re-implements what `materialize_llm_cost_name_edges` (protection.py:67) and `automatic_deletion_protections` (protection.py:86) already build: the `LLMCost-[:FOR_STANDARD_NAME]->StandardName` edge (`FOR_STANDARD_NAME`) and a multi-marker durable-authority aggregate over the same fields.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes one derivation rule rather than a spread of shallow wrappers, so no depth defect is visible in the design; the placement defect is reported under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan does not name, and would fork, two owners: origin recovery (imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:13875) and the catalog-import write guard (imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_import.py:52 + imas_codex/standard_names/protection.py:183).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no plan section adds a public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family, so there is no added surface for a section to account for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §1–§4 propose an origin-recovery rule and an import write guard without citing the existing machinery that already does both: `graph_ops.reconcile_catalog_edit_origins` (graph_ops.py:13875) and `catalog_import.record_catalog_import_provenance` (catalog_import.py:52).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan's §3 recovery rule is a parallel layer over the existing reconciler without stating why graph_ops.py:13875 cannot be extended.
